title: Grateful Dead Live at William and Mary College Hall on 1978-04-15
lineage: Sharp RT100 Deck [Master Cassette, Maxell XLII 90] > Sony PCM-M10 > Scandisc Ultra MicroSD 8gb [class 10]; Settings: Sharp RT100 Deck: Dolby NR - OFF & CrO2 - OFF; Settings: Sony PCM-M10 manual record level at 6; Recording Mode: LPCM [wav] 96.00kHz/24bit; Mastering & Editing: 96.00kHz/24bit wav > AA3 was used for +/- db gains, fade ins & outs; Converting Sample Rate: Adobe Audition 3.0 was also used to to convert 96.00kHz/24bit.WAV to sample rate to 44.10kHz/16bit with High Qulaity at 100%, Pre Post Filter checked, Dither enabled, Dither Depth at 1, P.D.F set to Triangular and No Noise Shaping; CD Wave Editor to Split Tracks & covert to Flac16 [Level 6]; TLH to fix SBE
source: Set 2 Source: sbd; Master tapes [were synced] - on a Aiwa CX-NA555 [using Maxell XLll 90 Type ll with High (CrO2 Tape OFF] NO Dolby; Tape

ai_review.summary: Decent soundboard recording but a short, sub‑par set with lukewarm vocals and a few bright moments.
ai_review.review: The board sounds pretty good, though the reviewer notes it could use a touch of reverb to soften the dry edge. Musically the show is described as one of the shortest and less than average, with marginal Jerry vocals and a disappointing ending to the R&R > One More Saturday Night sequence, yet the reviewer does highlight several enjoyable segments such as Bertha > Good Lovin', Candyman, El Paso, Let It Grow, and Not Fade Away > Morning Dew.

ai_rating.rationale: The single review rates the show 2 stars and calls it below average, while noting a decent soundboard; this yields a low overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear board recording but slightly dry; reviewer suggests adding a little reverb to soften it up.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is noted as unusually short and less than average, with a weak ending to the R&R > One More Saturday Night sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals are described as only marginal tonight.
